title: King Midas and the Golden Touch
text:
Silenus, the old companion of the god Bacchus, wandered off drunk and was found by Phrygian peasants, who brought him to their king, Midas. Midas welcomed him with ten days of feasting and then returned him safely to Bacchus. Grateful, the god offered Midas any reward he wished.

Midas asked that everything he touched should turn to gold. Bacchus granted it, though he was sorry Midas had not asked for something better.

Midas hurried off to test his gift. He broke a twig from an oak, and it turned to gold. He picked up a stone and a clod of earth, and they turned to gold. He plucked ears of grain and an apple, and they shone like treasure. He was overjoyed.

Then his servants set a meal before him. When he touched the bread, it hardened into gold. When he bit into meat, his teeth met gold. When he mixed wine with water and raised it to his lips, molten gold ran into his mouth. Rich and miserable, starving and parched, he raised his shining arms to the sky and begged Bacchus to take back the gift.

The god told him to go to the source of the river Pactolus and wash himself in it. Midas did, and the power passed from his body into the water. Ever since, the sands of that river have glittered with gold.
lesson: Before you ask for something, think through what it would mean to have it in every part of your life. An outcome that sounds perfect can carry costs you never pictured.
